newsitem.title: UK: Copper dives, worst of LME tightness may be over.
newsitem.headline: Copper dives, worst of LME tightness may be over.

text.p: A few hints that the worst of the supply tightness, that has been driving LME copper prices higher recently, may have passed prompted a late afternoon sell-off.
Three months delivery copper last traded at $2,437 a tonne, down $74 from Monday's close, after touching a five-week low of $2,430.

Traders said the failure of the market to convincingly pierce $2,600 earlier in the month, a narrowing in the spread, a few small warehouse stock increases and the approaching summer slow-down all combined to take the heat out of the buy side.
"Even today's news has not exactly been friendly for buyers,' one trader said.
He refered to news of an impending resumption of labour talks at Canadian producer Inco's strike-bound Sudbury, Ontario facilities, which produce around 100,000 tonnes of copper.
Also, Chile's El Teniente mine expected to return to normal operations on Tuesday after being closed at the week-end by heavy snowfall.
"None of these are earth-shattering developments but together they give you the feeling that perhaps we've seen the highs for the time being, a trader said.
As the selling built up, sell stops were triggered as chart points at $2,460 and $2,430 were pierced.
"The next support could be expected around $2,350 but major support is not until $2,245,' said Rudolf Wolff analyst William Adams.
Among other metals copper's sell-off caused a downward adjustment in zinc and aluminium.
Profittaking hit zinc which gave up the $1,400 level in the late afternoon to end at $1,397, down $11.5 from Monday.
But aluminium continued to disappoint its supporters, failing to test $1,490 resistance despite the continuing fall in LME warehouse stocks.
It succumbed to liquidation orders late in the day to finally trade at $1,577 a tonne, down $13.
Nickel drifted lower on the prospect of the Inco talks resuming and three months delivery ended the afternoon kerb trading at $7,170, down $40 from Monday.
Lead ended just below $620, down around $4, tin at $5,580, down $40, and alloy at $1,467, unchanged.
